The seventh review of 1.24.36 (the mends of adb8fd7, "the sixth review mended")
==============================================================================

SUMMARY

336 cases of my own (cases.js), replayed by replay.js against src/lantern.inner.html at adb8fd7 (run_adb8fd7.txt):
256 AGREE, 80 DISAGREE -- 45 high, 33 medium, 2 low. The same cases on 801fe71: 210 AGREE, 126 DISAGREE.
Between the two: 92 cases mended by the last round, 46 broken by it (13 high, 33 medium), 34 wrong in both.
(HEAD moved to 8f6c242 while I worked; it changes agent/ files only. src/lantern.inner.html is byte-for-byte
adb8fd7's, checked with cmp.)

The guards hold: every bench prompt other than make-control and make-control-b equals 1.24.35's (298 prompts), and
all 1591 saved replies with a MAKE block in tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json build as on 1.24.35
(guard_1235.json, made by gen_guard.js from 8cb3281's file).

Two of the last round's mends made new HIGH harm:
  - the transformer-pair rule takes a MOTOR's dual voltage for the control supply whenever "control transformer" is
    anywhere in the question;
  - stopSaid's new "<word> stop button" rule lets "a stop button for both conveyors" through to the sequence given.
Several other mends are right for the phrasings they were written from, and miss close variants (below).


HIGH -- a given shown for a question it does not fit, or fitted wrong; a kept circuit shown for another question

H1 (new in adb8fd7) A motor's dual voltage becomes the control supply. 7 cases:
   sup-motor-460-230-ct     "Draw a motor starter for a 460/230 V motor with a control transformer"   -> supply "230 V AC"
   sup-pump-480-240-ct      "... for a 480/240 V pump with a control transformer"                    -> supply "240 V AC"
   sup-motor-240-120-ct     "... for a 240/120 V single phase motor with a control transformer"      -> supply "120 V AC"
   sup-ct-for-motor         "... and a control transformer for the 460/230 V motor"                  -> supply "230 V AC"
   sup-fan-460-230-ct, sup-conv-480-240-ct, sup-motor-pair-ct-480-240 (the same)
   Right: no supply line -- the control voltage is not said (801fe71 gave none).
   Seen in supply(): with one pair and one voltage, the pair is taken as the transformer's if "control transformer" (or
   "transformer ... control") is anywhere in the question. The pair has to be the transformer's own: written against
   it ("480/120 V control transformer", "control transformer, 480/120 V"), and never a pair followed by motor, pump,
   fan, conveyor, compressor or "single phase".

H2 (new in adb8fd7) One stop for both machines, said after the button, gets the sequence given (a stop each). 6 cases:
   sq-stop-for-both          "... conveyor 2 can only start after conveyor 1 is running, with a stop button for both conveyors"
   sq-stop-common-to-both    "... with a stop button common to both"
   sq-stop-for-the-two       "... a stop push button for the two conveyors"
   sq-red-stop-for-both      "... with a red stop button for both"
   sq-stop-on-c1-for-both    "... with a stop button on conveyor 1 for both"
   sq-stop-pb-for-both-pumps "pump 2 ... with a stop pushbutton for both pumps"
   Right: no given (801fe71 gave none: "stop" stayed in the text). The given draws "conveyor 1 stop" and
   "conveyor 2 stop"; the question asks one stop for both.
   Seen in stopSaid(): rs.replace(/\b([a-z]+)\s+stop(...buttons?|pbs?)\b/, ...) takes out "a stop button" whatever
   follows it. Keep it where "for both", "for the two", "for all", "common to", "shared" follow (the words after the
   button, as well as the word before it, say whether it is one for all). "for each" is already handled.

H3 (in both) One start, the stops at two places: two stations given. 3 cases:
   st-one-start-stops-two     "Draw a motor starter with a start button and stop buttons at two locations"
   st-start-stops-two-places  "Draw a motor starter with a start and stops at two places"
   st-one-start-stops-two-b   "Draw a motor starter with one start button and stop buttons at two locations"
   Right: no given (2 stops, 1 start). The last round's window says start and stop both stand in the count's clause,
   but here the count is of the stops only. The word right before the count ("stop buttons at two locations") says
   whose it is: read the window from the last "and"/"with" (not only "and a/an/the/one/two..."), or require the
   start and the stop to be joined ("start/stop", "start and stop", "start-stop").

H4 (in both) The other machine OFF, said after a comma aside: a sequence given. 3 cases:
   sq-comma-off-feed   "conveyor 2 can only start when conveyor 1, its feed conveyor, is off"
   sq-comma-off-duty   "pump 2 can only start when pump 1, the duty pump, is off"
   sq-comma-off-other  "pump 1 can start only after pump 2, the other pump, is off"
   Right: no given (the given has the later machine start only WHILE the first runs -- the opposite).
   Seen in seqOrder(): rest = t.slice(Y.end).split(/[.;:?!,]/)[0] stops at the aside's comma. Read the clause to the
   sentence's end (or skip a ", ... ," aside) before deciding it says nothing of off.

H5 (in both) A second machine named "the motor": the delayed start given for one machine. 3 cases:
   dl-fan-after-motor        "Draw the control circuit for a fan that starts 10 seconds after the motor starts"
   dl-conv-after-motor       "... a conveyor that starts 5 seconds after the motor starts"
   dl-coolingfan-after-motor "... a cooling fan that starts 30 seconds after the motor starts"
   Right: no given. The given starts the fan from its own button after a delay; the question has the fan follow a
   motor the given does not draw. machines() leaves "motor" out of its count ("a pump motor" is one machine); "X starts
   ... after the motor (starts)" names two.

H6 (in both) A light in or on a button, said otherwise than the mend's phrasings. 5 cases:
   lt-stop-has-red-in-it     "a stop button that has a red light in it"   -> lamp LT1 M1 "run" red (a RUN light, red)
   lt-lamp-in-it             "a start button with a green lamp in it"     -> lamp LT1 M1 "run" green
   lt-light-up-start         "a light-up start button"                    -> lamp LT1 M1 "run" green
   lt-lit-up-start           "a green lit-up start button"                -> no lamp (the light asked for left out)
   lt-start-illuminated-after "... the start button illuminated"         -> no lamp
   Right: no given (the mend: a light in or on a button, or a button that lights up, gives none). "in it", "lit-up",
   "light-up", "illuminated" after the button are the same thing ("backlit" already gives none).

H7 (in both) A horn AND a light asked for the sump's alarm, the light named after the horn: horn only. 2 cases:
   su-horn-and-light-for-alarm  "a sump pump with a horn and a light for the high water alarm"
   su-horn-light-for-the-alarm  "a sump pump with a high water alarm horn and a light for the alarm"
   Right: no given, or the horn and the red high water light both (the mend's own aim). Seen: read() drops a light
   whose words after it say "alarm" (OTHERL), and al only knows "alarm light" / "high water light".

H8 (in both) One button that starts and stops, said otherwise than the mend's phrasings: a two-button starter. 7 cases:
   ob-same-pb-starts-stops  "where the same pushbutton starts and stops the motor"
   ob-push-again            "push the button to start and push it again to stop"
   ob-one-start-stop-button "with one start/stop button"
   ob-start-is-stop         "with a start button that is also the stop button"
   ob-push-to-start-stop    "with a push-to-start, push-to-stop button"
   ob-single-start-stop-pb  "with a single start-stop push button"
   ob-latching-pb           "with a latching push button" (a push-push button; the least sure of these)
   Right: no given. The starter's `not` knows "same button", "(one|single) (push)button", "also stops",
   "push on push off"; "same pushbutton", "one start/stop button", "again to stop", "is also the stop" pass.

H9 (in both; the last round's "same question" rule misses it) Kept circuits shown for the plural. 7 cases:
   kp-plural-pumps     kept "Draw a start stop circuit for the pump"      shown for "... for the pumps"
   kp-plural-conveyors kept "Draw a motor starter for the conveyor"       shown for "Draw motor starters for the conveyors"
   kp-plural-fans      kept "Draw a fan starter with an e-stop"           shown for "Draw fan starters with an e-stop"
   kp-plural-well-pumps, kp-plural-estops ("with e-stops": Lantern's own givens refuse e-stops in the plural),
   kp-plural-stations ("start/stop stations"), kp-plural-floats ("with floats": Lantern's own refuse floats)
   Right: hidden. said() passes every word through stem(), which drops a plural s; "the same question, its words in
   the same order" then holds for pump/pumps, station/stations, float/floats, e-stop/e-stops. Compare said() words
   unstemmed (only the asking words dropped).
   The same plural reaches Lantern's own starter given (2 cases, gv-plural-pumps "Draw a start stop circuit for the
   pumps", gv-plural-fans "... for the fans": one pump, one fan drawn). machines() counts "pumps" only after a number.


MEDIUM -- a clear miss of a plain question that 801fe71 got right (all 33 are new in adb8fd7)

M1 A control voltage said in so many words is dropped whenever a pair stands anywhere in the question. 11 cases:
   sup-twoV-slash ("a 480 V / 120 V control transformer"), sup-twoV-24 ("a 240 V / 24 V control transformer" -- the
   mend's own example, said to be a control transformer's), sup-twoV-nospace ("480V/120V"), sup-paren ("a 120 V control
   transformer (480 V to 120 V)"), sup-motor-pair-ctrl ("a 230/460 V pump motor with 120 V control"),
   sup-motor-range-ctrl ("a 208-230 V pump with a 24 V control circuit"), sup-motor-277 ("a 480/277 V motor and a 120 V
   control transformer"), sup-supply-400-230 ("230 V control from a 400/230 V supply"), sup-tx-480-240-ctrl,
   sup-ct-pair-and-motor-volt ("a 480/120 V control transformer for a 460 V motor"), sup-motor-pair-ct-120.
   Right: the control supply 801fe71 gave (120 V AC, 24 V AC, 230 V AC ...). Seen: `if (pr.length)` returns null unless
   exactly one voltage and one pair; a dual-voltage motor ("230/460 V") is common in exactly these questions. Let the
   pair rule decide only the pair's own voltage, and fall through to the CTRL_AFTER/CTRL_BEFORE reading otherwise; two
   voltages both written with V around a "/" or "to" next to "control transformer" are the same pair.

M2 The station count's window refuses a plain count. 4 cases:
   st-estop-before      "a motor starter with an e-stop and start/stop buttons at two locations"
   st-runlight-before   "a pump starter with a run light and start/stop at two locations"
   st-greenlight-before "a motor starter with a green run light and start/stop stations at two locations"
   st-stop-two-start-two "with a stop button at two locations and a start button at two locations"
   Right: two stations (and the e-stop, the light). Seen: the window runs back to "with" because "and start/stop" is no
   cut ("and" is a cut only before a/an/the/one/two...), so the e-stop or the light before it is in the window. The
   last two: each half said at two places, cut apart by "and a".

M3 The delayed start refuses its own plain questions. 5 cases:
   dl-horn-comes-on          "press start, the warning horn comes on for 10 seconds, then the conveyor starts"
   dl-light-comes-on-runs    "... with a green light that comes on while the pump runs"
   dl-start-stop-estop-commas "... with start, stop and e-stop, starting 5 seconds after start is pressed"
   dl-stops-when-stop        "... starts 10 seconds after start, and stops when stop is pressed"
   dl-stop-button-stops      "... ; the stop button stops the pump"
   Right: the delayed start (801fe71 gave it, with the horn or the run light). "comes on" is refused anywhere, not only
   where power or the light is what the start waits for; stopSaid() reads "start, stop" (a comma between) and the stop
   button stopping its own machine as a stop said otherwise.

M4 Words read as a vacuum: the cut-out is no longer judged. 5 cases:
   cc-120vac-cutout-no "an air compressor, 120 VAC control, with a high pressure cut-out" (written open: not sent back)
   cc-24vac-cutin-out-no ("24 VAC control transformer"), cc-120vac-label (VAC in the switch's label), cc-vacation ("our
   vacation cabin"), cc-negative-dc-rail ("24 V DC control with the negative rail grounded").
   Right: sent back with "pressure PS1 M1 nc ..." as 801fe71 did. /\bvac\w*/ matches VAC and vacation; \bnegative\b a
   DC rail. Use \bvacuum\b|\bvac\b(?!\w) not after a number (\d\s*vac), and "negative pressure".

M5 "overload" in a starter's own name makes it no machine. 4 cases:
   cc-ol-no-label-overload ("coil M1 \"pump starter with overload\"", overload written no: not sent back),
   cc-cutout-label-overload ("compressor starter and overload"), cc-cutout-starter-overload-protected ("starter M1
   \"overload protected compressor starter\""), cc-ol-no-starter-overload-relay-label.
   Right: judged as 801fe71 did. A relay named for an overload is not a machine; a starter (kind starter, or MACHINE in
   its name) named with its overload still is: test NOT_MACHINE's overload only where nothing else names a machine.

M6 A stop written "no" on a run relay is not judged when the relay's closed contact is used anywhere. 4 cases:
   cc-stop-no-run-relay-stopped-lamp (lamp LT1 CR1 off "stopped"), cc-stop-no-k1-ready-lamp, cc-stop-no-delayed-ready
   (Lantern's own delayed start with a ready light), cc-stop-no-run-relay-idle-relay (coil CR2 CR1 off "idle relay").
   Right: sent back ("stop PB1 CR1"), as 801fe71 did: the relay seals itself through its start, so it is a run relay.
   The trip relay the mend was for drives the STOPPED machine's coil from its closed contact and has no start of its
   own; ask that (no start on the relay, or the nc contact in the rung of a coil the stop's relay is meant to drop),
   not "any nc contact anywhere" -- a lamp's rung never makes it a trip relay.


LOW

L1 pk-lusaka-zambia, pk-harare-zimbabwe: Zambia and Zimbabwe are in PLACE_IEC's list but not in its comma form
   ("Lusaka, Zambia" follows US). The reference shown changes, nothing drawn.


WHAT AGREES (256 cases)

- Control transformer pairs written against the transformer: 480/120, 480 to 120, 480-120, 600/120, 208/120, 480/24,
  120/24, "control transformer, 480/120 V", 480/240; not-sure pairs (no "control", 24/120, "120 V/24", "fed from a
  480/120 V transformer") give no supply line; 24 V DC, 120 VAC coil.
- Stations: two/three, local and remote, two and two buttons, "started and stopped from two places", "one at each
  end", the e-stop or light after the count; none for an e-stop, a light or a pilot at two locations, stops at two and
  one start, start at two and stop at one, "stopped from two", "plus a stop at the machine", "the start at one",
  "only from the panel".
- Sequences: 19 right givens (numbers, letters, M tags, first/second, before, unless, interlock, in sequence, a run
  light each, one e-stop, a stop for each); none for off, idle, down, not running, stopped, finished, turned or switched
  off, if off; none with no permissive word (first ... then, once running); none for a common, master, single, shared,
  in-series stop, "halts both", "conveyor 1's stop stops both", a stopped light each.
- Delayed start: none with no time, for "time delay relay" or "on-delay timer" alone, two times, "released", an
  off-delay too, a 3 s horn against a 5 s start, "waits then stops", power restored, "a delay relay that stops it";
  given for "wait 5 seconds, then the motor runs", 2 h.p., warning horns, buzzer until it starts, e-stop, run light,
  24 V DC.
- Lights: none for a light in, inside or on a button, a button that lights up, glows or is lit, "lights a red light";
  run, stopped and both lights; sump alarms with a light, a horn, both (alarm light / high water light / buzzer); none
  for a plain light beside the alarm.
- E-stop: none for a mushroom head not said to be an emergency stop; mushroom e-stops given; none for push on push
  off, "also stops", single pushbutton, "one button both starts and stops", "same button for start and stop", toggle,
  e-stops at each station.
- Sizes: "2 h.p.", "7.5 h.p.", "1/2 h.p.", "2 h. p.", "2 H.P." no longer read as hours; "runs for 2 hours" still is.
- Code checks: vacuum, inHg and negative-pressure switches not judged; a trip relay's stop not judged (both forms);
  cut-outs, overloads and stops written open are sent back with the line; Lantern's own givens (compressor, sump with
  alarm, two-float fill, reversing, delayed start with horn) built as shown are never sent back; every given shown by
  a case built clean.
- Kept circuits: shown for the same question (please, again, a/the, e-stop/emergency stop); hidden for the other
  colour, without the light, no e-stop, each pump, 24 V AC/DC, can/can't, swapped colours, an "explain" question, a
  circuit kept with no question.
- Which code: Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Pakistan, Egypt, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the UAE, Dubai,
  Kenya, Nigeria, Korea in place and comma forms pick IEC (and the line goes back "IEC practice: IEC 60204-1:2016,
  9.3.2"); Mexico in both forms, New Mexico, Egypt Road in Ohio, Dubai Street in Texas pick US; an IEC contactor at
  480 V 60 Hz is US, a NEMA starter at 400 V 50 Hz IEC.
- The guards (bench prompts, saved MAKE replies) as on 1.24.35.


WHAT WAS NOT RUN

- npm test, the browser tests and any model: as asked. The cases run in jsdom through load.js only.
- No bench run (the 35B, 4B, 2B or 0.8B): nothing here says how a model copies these blocks.
- Kept circuits were kept with L.givens.keep() directly, not through the "Keep as my given" button; the code choice
  button (choose()) and the view under a drawing were not exercised; a kept circuit shown to a pump-station question
  (PROMPT_PUMPS, user-only) was not tried.
- Drawings were not looked at: a block that builds clean was not checked by eye.
- I did not read tests/fixtures/givens_review_1236/, givens_review2_1236/, code_checks_review_1236/, review3_1236/ to
  review6_1236/, tests/givens_1236.js, tests/code_checks_1236.js or tests/review*_1236.py: some of my cases may repeat
  theirs.
